info.name: Atlas — Workflow Engine API
info.description:
# Atlas — Workflow Engine API

Everything you need to drive a running **Atlas** BPMN workflow engine from Postman: deploy models, run instances, inspect live runtime, work user-task inboxes, and correlate messages.

## Prerequisites

You need a running server. From the repo root:

```bash
go run ./cmd/atlas serve --addr :8080 --data-dir ./atlas-data
```

The API is served under `/api/v1`, the web UI at `/`, and the MCP transport at `/mcp`. Health lives at `/healthz`.

## Setup (30 seconds)

1. **Import** this collection **and** the `Atlas (local)` environment (`Atlas.postman_environment.json`).
2. **Select** the `Atlas (local)` environment (top-right in Postman).
3. Confirm `baseUrl` points at your server (default `http://localhost:8080`).
4. Open **🚀 Golden Path** and hit **Send** on each request top to bottom — or run the folder in the **Collection Runner**.

## How the chaining works

Requests capture ids into **collection variables** (`defKey`, `instanceKey`, `taskKey`, `projectId`, …) in their *Tests* tab, so downstream requests like `{{defKey}}` resolve automatically. No copy-paste of keys between steps.

## Authentication

The Atlas server is **unauthenticated** by design — it expects to sit behind a reverse proxy that adds auth. If yours does, add the header/token under the collection's **Authorization** tab and it applies to every request. Out of the box, no credentials are needed.

## Conventions

- **Deploy** bodies are raw **BPMN XML** (`Content-Type: application/xml`).
- Everything else is **JSON**. Variables use `{"variables": {name: value}}`; scalars, objects, and arrays are all supported and bind into FEEL.
- Keys are `uint64`, assigned by the engine and returned on deploy/list.

item.name: 🚀 Golden Path (run top-to-bottom)
item.description:
The five-minute tour. Hit **Send** on each request in order — or select this folder in the **Collection Runner** and run it — and it walks the full workflow lifecycle end to end.

Each step's *Tests* tab captures ids (`defKey`, `taskKey`) into collection variables, so the next step just works with no copy-paste.

1. Deploy a BPMN model
2. List processes (confirm it's registered)
3. Start an instance
4. List open user tasks (parks on *Review order*)
5. Complete the task with form data
6. List instances (see the variables land)
7. Read engine stats

request.description:
Deploy the bundled `order-approval` model (raw BPMN 2.0 XML in the body). The response echoes the assigned definition **key**, `processId`, and `version`; a collaboration lists one entry per pool under `deployments`.

Captures `defKey` for the next steps.

body.raw:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<definitions xmlns="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL"
             xmlns:zeebe="http://camunda.org/schema/zeebe/1.0">
  <process id="order-approval" isExecutable="true">
    <startEvent id="start"/>
    <userTask id="review" name="Review order">
      <extensionElements>
        <zeebe:assignmentDefinition candidateGroups="reviewers"/>
      </extensionElements>
    </userTask>
    <userTask id="approve" name="Approve order">
      <extensionElements>
        <zeebe:assignmentDefinition candidateGroups="managers"/>
      </extensionElements>
    </userTask>
    <endEvent id="end"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="f1" sourceRef="start" targetRef="review"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="f2" sourceRef="review" targetRef="approve"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="f3" sourceRef="approve" targetRef="end"/>
  </process>
</definitions>

request.description: Every deployed definition in registration order. Your freshly deployed `order-approval` should appear with the `defKey` from step 1.

Start one instance of the deployed definition, optionally seeded with start variables. The engine runs it to idle; `order-approval` parks on the first user task.

Body: `{"variables": {...}}` (scalars, objects, and arrays are all accepted; numbers keep exact decimal form).

Open user tasks (activatable user-task jobs) across all instances, with their assignment metadata (`assignee`, `candidateGroups`, `formId`).

Captures the first task's key as `taskKey`.

exec: pm.test('at least one open task', () => pm.expect(tasks.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description: Complete the captured user task, submitting form data as `{"variables": {...}}`. Those variables are written into the instance scope exactly like a service-task worker's outputs. The instance then advances to the next task (*Approve order*).

Live instances (with their current token count) followed by finished ones, most-recently-completed first. Each row carries its variables — you'll see the `approved`/`score`/`note` values from step 5 plus the start variables from step 3.
Live engine counts: active process instances and active element instances (tokens). A quick liveness/throughput probe.

item.name: Health & Info
item.description: Liveness and metadata — no state changes.

request.description: Plain-text `ok` liveness probe. Returns 200 as soon as the server is accepting traffic.
Product name and version (`{"product":"Atlas","version":...}`).
Active process-instance and element-instance (token) counts.

item.name: FEEL Playground
item.description: Compile and evaluate FEEL expressions with the *same* engine deployment uses — handy for authoring gateway conditions and mappings before deploying. Pure compile/eval: no engine state is touched.

request.description: Compile-only check. `{"ok":true}` on success, `{"ok":false,"error":...}` on a parse/type error. Unknown identifiers are allowed (they're process variables). An empty expression is a no-op success.

Compile **and** evaluate against sample variables. Returns `{"ok":true,"result":...,"kind":...}`. Objects/arrays bind as FEEL contexts/lists; numbers keep exact decimals. A FEEL type error evaluates to `null` rather than failing.

item.name: Deployments & Processes
item.description: Deploy BPMN models and inspect the resulting definitions. Deployments are durable (an on-disk sidecar) and survive a restart.

request.description: Deploy raw BPMN 2.0 XML. Compiles and registers every executable process in the model — one for a plain model, one per pool for a collaboration. 400 if the model doesn't compile.

body.raw:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<definitions xmlns="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL"
             xmlns:zeebe="http://camunda.org/schema/zeebe/1.0">
  <process id="order-approval" isExecutable="true">
    <startEvent id="start"/>
    <userTask id="review" name="Review order">
      <extensionElements>
        <zeebe:assignmentDefinition candidateGroups="reviewers"/>
      </extensionElements>
    </userTask>
    <userTask id="approve" name="Approve order">
      <extensionElements>
        <zeebe:assignmentDefinition candidateGroups="managers"/>
      </extensionElements>
    </userTask>
    <endEvent id="end"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="f1" sourceRef="start" targetRef="review"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="f2" sourceRef="review" targetRef="approve"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="f3" sourceRef="approve" targetRef="end"/>
  </process>
</definitions>

request.description: All deployed definitions in registration order, each with `key`, `processId`, `name`, `version`, `deployedAt`, and `collaborationKey` (non-zero for a collaboration pool).
The original BPMN XML of a definition. If the model carried no diagram layout, a generated left-to-right layout is injected so it still renders. 404 for an unknown key.
Per-element live token counts and visit history for one definition — the data the live viewer overlays on the diagram. Optional `?instance=<key>` narrows to a single instance.
Whole-collaboration runtime for the replay view: pools, merged element overlay across pools, and the time-ordered message flows between them. The path key may be any pool of the collaboration.
Remove one deployed definition (version). 409 if it still has running instances — cancel them first. 204 on success.

item.name: Instances
item.description: Start, list, and cancel process instances.

request.description: Start one instance, optionally seeded with `{"variables": {...}}`. Runs to idle and returns the resulting live counts. An empty body `{}` starts with no variables.
Live instances (with token counts) then finished ones (most-recently-completed first). Each row carries its variables.
Terminate a running instance (e.g. one parked on a wait that will never complete). It moves to the finished list as `terminated`. 404 if no active instance has that key.

item.name: User Tasks
item.description: The human-task inbox: list open user tasks, claim/unclaim them, and complete them with form data.

request.description: Open user tasks across all instances, with `assignee`, `candidateGroups`, and `formId` metadata.
Assign an open task to a person. Body `{"assignee": "..."}`. Claiming an already-claimed task reassigns it (last-writer-wins). 400 on empty assignee, 404 if the task is gone/completed.
Release a task (clears the assignee), making it available again. 404 if the task is gone/completed.
Complete a user task, optionally submitting form data as `{"variables": {...}}` written into the instance scope. An empty body completes with no variables. 404 if the task is gone/completed.

item.name: Messages
item.description: Correlate a message into waiting instances.

request.description: Publish a message by `name` + `correlationKey`, with optional `variables`. Correlates against open subscriptions and runs the engine to idle so any waiting instance advances. A message that matches nothing is accepted as a no-op (no buffering yet).

item.name: Projects, Drafts, Forms & DMN (Modeler)
item.description: Artifacts the browser Modeler manages: projects grouping work, saved-but-not-deployed diagrams (drafts), form definitions, and DMN references. Mostly used by the UI, exposed here for completeness and automation.

request.description: Create a project (a named grouping for artifacts). Body `{"name": "..."}`.
All projects with their artifact counts.
Rename a project. Body `{"name": "..."}`.
Dry-run the project's deployable bundle: compiles each diagram and resolves its DMN references, reporting problems without deploying.
Deploy the project's bundle: every diagram plus its resolved DMN models, so business rule tasks actually evaluate at runtime.
Delete a project.
Persist a diagram as a draft (raw BPMN, stored as-is WITHOUT compiling), keyed by its `<process id>`. Re-saving the same id overwrites. Optional `?projectId=` files it into a project.

body.raw:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<definitions xmlns="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL"
             xmlns:zeebe="http://camunda.org/schema/zeebe/1.0">
  <process id="order-approval" isExecutable="true">
    <startEvent id="start"/>
    <userTask id="review" name="Review order">
      <extensionElements>
        <zeebe:assignmentDefinition candidateGroups="reviewers"/>
      </extensionElements>
    </userTask>
    <userTask id="approve" name="Approve order">
      <extensionElements>
        <zeebe:assignmentDefinition candidateGroups="managers"/>
      </extensionElements>
    </userTask>
    <endEvent id="end"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="f1" sourceRef="start" targetRef="review"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="f2" sourceRef="review" targetRef="approve"/>
    <sequenceFlow id="f3" sourceRef="approve" targetRef="end"/>
  </process>
</definitions>

request.description: Saved drafts, most-recently-saved first. Optional `?projectId=` narrows to one project.
A draft's raw BPMN XML, so the editor can reopen it. `draftId` is the `<process id>`.
Reassign a draft to another project (empty `projectId` = Ungrouped). Body `{"projectId": "..."}`.
Remove a draft. Idempotent — deleting an absent draft still succeeds.
Create/replace a form definition (form-js schema) bound to user tasks. Body `{"id","name","projectId","schema": {...}}`.
All form definitions (metadata).
One form definition, including its schema.
Delete a form definition.
Register a reference to a DMN model (resolved from the temis model service or the local dmn-models folder). Body `{"name","modelRef","projectId"}`.
All DMN reference artifacts.
Resolve and temis-compile the referenced DMN model, reporting whether it's deployable.
Reassign a DMN reference to another project. Body `{"projectId": "..."}`.
Delete a DMN reference artifact.

item.name: MCP (AI agents)
item.description:
The same server also speaks the **Model Context Protocol** over Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, so an AI agent (e.g. a claude.ai custom connector) can drive it with the `atlas_*` tools. These are JSON-RPC 2.0 calls — included so you can poke the transport from Postman.

⚠️ The `/mcp` endpoint is UNAUTHENTICATED; put auth in front of it before exposing it publicly.

request.description: JSON-RPC `initialize` handshake. Note the `Accept` header must allow both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`.
JSON-RPC `tools/list` — enumerate the `atlas_*` tools the adapter exposes.
JSON-RPC `tools/call` invoking `atlas_stats` — the MCP equivalent of `GET /api/v1/stats`.
